uncited: Debug and Visualization methods render explicit geometric primitives (boxes, lines, or spheres) derived from voxel data to inspect spatial distribution, verify data loading, and provide visual context for volume extents.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Binary Volume Rendering](1015-binary-volume-rendering.md) or [Naive Voxel Rendering](1103-naive-voxel-rendering.md) by focusing on auxiliary debugging aids (wireframes, occupancy spheres) rather than the final volumetric appearance.
**Primitive Generation**: Each occupied voxel or volume extent is represented by one or more geometric primitives.
**Coordinate Transformation**: Voxel indices $(i, j, k)$ are transformed into world space.
**Rasterization**: The generated primitives are transformed into clip space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix and rasterized.
**Culling**: To manage performance, frustum culling is applied to exclude voxels outside the camera view.
The techniques described in this family are primarily found in custom graphics engines and research prototypes for real-time volume inspection.
These methods are essential for validating the correctness of voxelization, sparse storage, and ray-marching algorithms before integrating them into final rendering passes.
